10.1002_aenm.202506191: Aqueous zinc ion batteries (AZIBs) hold enormous potential as novel energy devices in light of their high safety, reasonable cost, and eco‐economic. While their application on a wide scale is restricted by the notorious dendrite growth and side reactions at the Zn anode/electrolyte interface. Herin, a dynamic regulation of interfacial micro‐environment strategy is proposed, introducing a green and safe hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) electrolyte additive to build highly stable and reversible Zn anode. Experiment and calculation results demonstrate that HEC can preferentially adsorb on Zn anode surface and create an HEC‐rich transition layer in inner Helmholtz plane (IHP) during plating/stripping. This layer can shield the parasitic reactions induced by active water and facilitate Zn uniform deposition. Meanwhile, HEC can reconstruct the Zn 2+ solvation sheath in outer Helmholtz plane (OHP), which accelerates Zn 2+ desolvation kinetics. Consequently, the Zn//Zn cells containing HEC electrolyte additive cycle stably for 2300 h and over 350 h at 1 and 30 mA cm −2 , respectively. It also endows Zn anode with excellent reversibility, maintaining high Coulombic efficiency of 99.4% over 600 cycles. After 3000 cycles, the Zn//AC@MnO 2 full cell with HEC electrolyte additive continues to exhibit outstanding cycling performance, retaining 85.2% of its initial capacity.
10.1016_j.apsusc.2026.167263: This study explores the development of microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) composites functionalized with conducting polymers and silver nanoparticles for sustainable electrochemical biosensing. The research focused on understanding the influence of polyaniline (PANI), polyethylene glycol (PEG), and silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) on the electrical conductivity of these composites. Using a Design of Experiments approach and a cubic Scheffé mixture model, the team systematically examined various compositions and built a predictive conductivity model. The model, with strong statistical performance (R² = 0.8549), identified aniline as the most crucial factor, with pure PANI achieving a conductivity of 1.4 × 10⁻³ S/cm. An optimized blend with less aniline and balanced PEG and AgNO₃ levels achieved nearly the same conductivity (1.1 × 10⁻³ S/cm), demonstrating PEG's key role in stabilizing and dispersing AgNPs. Model validation showed excellent predictive accuracy, with errors under 15%. Characterization methods, such as scanning electron microscopy and infrared spectroscopy, confirmed a uniform distribution of AgNPs and favorable component interactions. The optimized MFC-based composite offers a sustainable, tunable platform for sensitive electrochemical biosensing with controlled, predictable electrical.
10.1016_j.enceco.2026.10.017: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as a critical environmental threat to the East China Sea. Nevertheless, existing studies highlight a notable data gap regarding the distribution patterns of MPs in marine sediment, not to mention the associated ecological risks. This study revealed the distribution patterns of MPs in offshore and open sea sediments of the East China Sea by combining laser direct infrared spectroscopy and pyrolysis-gas chromatography–mass spectrometry. Concurrently, the microbial communities were characterized, and the synergistic ecological impacts of MPs and the environmental features on microbial community were analyzed using Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA). Results demonstrated that MPs pollution in the East China Sea sediment is on par with global marine pollution levels (mean concentration of 86.86 mg/kg dw) and the offshore regions are facing more serious situation. MPs also markedly suppressed microbial diversity, as evidenced by reduced community composition and altered function. Furthermore, WGCNA identified a complex interactive network between MPs and environmental features, which amplified the detrimental impacts on microbial communities. Collectively, these findings provide novel insights into the distribution characteristics of MPs in the East China Sea sediment and establish a comprehensive sedimentary microbial response for evaluating the ecological risks posed by the co-occurring environmental features and MPs. Statement of significance Microplastics (MPs) are critical challenges but their ecological effects on the East China Sea remain uncertain. Herein, MPs pollution in the East China Sea sediment and the negative impacts on microbial communities, synergy with environmental features, were evaluated. The findings suggested that the East China Sea was facing MPs pollution and pollution in offshore regions was more serious. MPs and environmental features co-occurringly suppressed microbial diversity. This work clarified MPs pollution in the East China Sea and evaluated the combined risks of MPs and environmental features to sedimentary microbial communities.
10.1021_acsami.6c04175: Sodium vanadium phosphate [Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 ] stands out as an appealing cathode material for next-generation sodium-ion batteries owing to beneficial properties, such as high operating voltage, fast ion diffusion, and robust structural integrity. Nonetheless, its commercialization is challenged by an inherently poor electronic conductivity. Herein, a europium 3+ (Eu 3+ ) doping strategy was employed to synthesize a Na 3 V 1.95 Eu 0.05 (PO 4 ) 3 @C composite (Eu0.05-NVP@C), aiming to enhance its high-rate capability and cycling durability. Based on electrochemical kinetic studies and theoretical computations, the introduction of Eu 3+ into Eu0.05-NVP@C effectively reduces the band gap and activation energy for Na + migration, which synergistically promotes faster charge transfers. Moreover, the smaller integrated crystal orbital Hamilton population values for the V–O and Eu–O bonds indicate enhanced lattice cohesion. Consequently, the fabricated Eu0.05-NVP@C cathode exhibits a high reversible capacity of 97.63 mAh g –1 at 10C and achieves 93.60% capacity retention after 2000 cycles at 5C. In situ X-ray diffraction analysis further reveals the highly reversible biphasic transition reaction during cycling. This work not only validates Eu 3+ doping as an effective approach for optimizing NASICON-type cathodes but also offers strategic guidance for the development of next-generation Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 -based electrodes with a superior rate performance and extended cycle life.
10.1021_acsami.6c18277: Electrocatalytic water splitting provides a sustainable route for hydrogen production, but alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) still suffer from sluggish kinetics and large polarization losses. Herein, a self-supported VS2-V2O5(x:y)@NF composite electrode was constructed through a stepwise hydrothermal strategy. In this design, vertically grown VS2 on nickel foam provides a conductive and open scaffold, while V2O5-derived oxygen-containing domains are introduced into the surface and inter-array spaces to increase accessible reaction sites and regulate the local adsorption environment. Among the investigated compositions, VS2-V2O5(1:1)@NF exhibits the most balanced bifunctional response within the sample series, requiring overpotentials of 272.2 mV for HER and 292.8 mV for OER at 10 mA cm-2 in 1 M KOH. In a two-electrode overall water-splitting configuration, the symmetric electrolyzer requires cell voltages of 1.88 V and 2.27 V to deliver 10 and 100 mA cm-2, respectively. The performance variation among the samples prepared with different V2O5 precursor-feeding amounts is correlated with the self-supported sulfide/oxide architecture, electrochemically accessible interface, apparent charge-transfer behavior, wettability, and surface reconstruction. The present results do not directly establish Fermi-level equilibration or quantitative interfacial charge redistribution.
